s00-01-pivot-2e9082.wav.text: It's one of the shortest commandments in the whole Bible.

s00-02-story-0fc5a4.wav.text: In English, it's just four words.

s00-04-talk-33280b.wav.text: Most of us read that and relax.

s00-07-pivot-7710f2.wav.text: But the Bible asks a much bigger question.

s00-08-story-dae712.wav.text: Not only what did you take? But what are your hands for?

s01-01-story-8b1514.wav.text: When Israel heard these words at Sinai, they were a nation of freed slaves.

s01-03-story-2e1712.wav.text: But God was bringing them to a land.

s01-04-story-a17c6e.wav.text: And every family would get a share of it. A field.

s01-06-talk-5427ba.wav.text: So when God says do not steal, he is guarding what he gave to your neighbor.

s01-07-talk-0b40dd.wav.text: Stealing grabs what God handed to someone else.

s02-01-pivot-71871c.wav.text: And the first time Israel entered that land, someone broke it.

s02-02-story-ae066e.wav.text: At Jericho, God told them that everything in the city was devoted to him.

s02-03-story-a72f74.wav.text: Nobody was to keep any of it.

s02-04-story-3e6866.wav.text: But a man named Achan saw a beautiful cloak, and some silver, and a bar of gold.

s02-06-grave-77abfd.wav.text: I coveted them and took them.

s02-07-grave-1a1a8c.wav.text: And see, they are hidden in the earth inside my tent, with the silver underneath.

s02-09-story-9e8ca4.wav.text: He saw. He wanted. He took. He hid.

s02-10-talk-cf1534.wav.text: The theft happened with his hands.

s02-11-story-de180d.wav.text: But it started in his heart.

s03-01-talk-e4e654.wav.text: Most stealing doesn't look like a robbery.

s03-02-story-ee7100.wav.text: It looks like Achan's tent: small, hidden, and easy to explain.

s03-03-story-a6b198.wav.text: Copying someone's homework. Keeping the extra change.

s03-05-talk-1e3ba3.wav.text: Nobody sees it, but it's still stealing.

s04-02-story-d57f28.wav.text: God's law doesn't stop at don't take.

s04-03-story-178c35.wav.text: Farmers in Israel weren't allowed to harvest right up to the edges of their fields,

s04-04-story-bb9513.wav.text: or pick up every fallen grape.

s04-05-grave-2f0eb8.wav.text: You shall leave them for the poor and for the sojourner: I am the LORD your God.

s04-06-talk-18ba3c.wav.text: Christians have long read this as the other side of the eighth commandment.

s04-07-story-2d9681.wav.text: Holding on too tightly can be a kind of taking too.

s05-01-pivot-d4796d.wav.text: Centuries later, Jesus walked into Jericho.

s05-02-story-98b123.wav.text: The same city where Achan stole.

s05-03-story-38d52d.wav.text: A tax collector lived there named Zacchaeus.

s05-04-story-de0c75.wav.text: He was rich, and everyone knew how he got that way.

s05-05-story-7dff2a.wav.text: He climbed a tree just to see Jesus.

s05-06-story-e72de8.wav.text: Jesus said he was coming to his house.

s05-07-story-f95816.wav.text: And Zacchaeus stood up and said this.

s05-08-grave-7b18f5.wav.text: Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor.

s05-09-grave-d9f889.wav.text: And if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I restore it fourfold.

s05-11-story-c02a08.wav.text: Zacchaeus gave back four times over.

s06-01-talk-4f3301.wav.text: The apostle Paul put it this way, writing to Christians in Ephesus.

s06-02-grave-ff5e08.wav.text: Let the thief no longer steal, but rather let him labor, doing honest work with his own hands,

s06-03-grave-3a8ab7.wav.text: so that he may have something to share with anyone in need.

s06-05-story-d53acc.wav.text: Not with stop taking, but with share.

s06-06-grave-f3c585.wav.text: The opposite of stealing isn't just keeping your hands to yourself.

s07-01-story-b4798f.wav.text: The God who gave every family its field is a giving God.

s07-02-talk-422b1c.wav.text: So the real question isn't only have I ever stolen?

s07-03-story-79d2e9.wav.text: It's what are my hands for?

s07-04-grave-b4af33.wav.text: Hands that once took can learn to give.

s07-05-talk-212276.wav.text: Next time, the ninth commandment: what happens when we steal someone's good name.
